=== F1 (NON-BLOCKING, and a real defect in NEW code). The auto-queue treats a
    proof record that says "UNCHECKED" as a satisfied proof gate. ===
scripts/lwb_auto_queue.py readiness() tests the proof record with exactly
three predicates: the record exists, its "pr" equals the PR number, and
checked_by != author. proof/29.json on this very branch reads
    "author":     "lw-architect-opus5-af50c414-2026-09-19"
    "checked_by": "UNCHECKED-pending-independent-review"
Reproduced by running that predicate against the real file: it produces NO
reasons -- the gate is satisfied. A record whose checked_by field literally
spells out that nobody has checked it is accepted as a checked record,
because the only question asked is whether the two strings differ. This is
the shape the brief tells me to hunt: code that cannot tell "I checked and
found nothing" from "I could not check". It is in this PR's own new code, it
is against this PR's own proof record, and the surrounding test file does
have test_a_self_certified_proof_record_blocks -- which covers only the
checked_by == author case, not this one. Not blocking on its own because the
workflow ships disabled and dry-run, but it should not be armed as written.
Suggested fix: reject a checked_by that is empty, equal to author, or matches
a placeholder/UNCHECKED shape, and require it to parse as an identity in the
same format reviews/README.md mandates for reviewer_id.

=== F2 (NON-BLOCKING). The vacuity meta-test does not exercise the guard, and
    the guard accepts any ref at all. ===
tests/test_lwb_auto_queue.py::test_that_guard_actually_fails_when_the_hazard_is_introduced
does not call the guard. It re-implements the guard's predicate inline over a
hand-built dict, then asserts the copy behaves. If the real guard above it
were weakened, this meta-test would keep passing -- it is a test of a
duplicate, not a mutation probe of the thing. Separately, the guard's
condition is `not (step.get("with") or {}).get("ref")`, i.e. it asks only
whether a ref is PRESENT, never what it says. A checkout pinned to
`ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}` -- pull-request-controlled
code, the exact hazard -- satisfies it. This repeats a finding an earlier
reviewer on this branch already made at 8a83970; the commit that answered the
two blocking findings (ae29b1a) did not change it. I confirmed it by reading
the current file, not from the earlier record.
